newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-MASTERS CHAMPION FALDO WORKS ON HIS PUTTING.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MASTERS CHAMPION FALDO WORKS ON HIS PUTTING.

text.p: Defending champion Nick Faldo, who has won the Masters three times, knows what it takes to win at Augusta National -- exceptional putting.

Faldo, who added last year's title to his 1989 amd 1990 victories, said on Monday he would be mainly working on his putting as he prepares for Thursday's opening round, when he will begin his quest to become the only golfer to win back-to-back Masters twice.

"I'm here to work on my putting. I've been doing that all (last) week," Faldo, 39, said as he barely missed a stride on his way from Augusta's pristine clubhouse to its huge practice green, which was surrounded by hundreds of sun-splashed spectators.
Faldo, who regularly plays the U.S. tour these days, skipped last week's event in New Orleans to work on his putting with his long-time coach, David Leadbetter.
"Led's been helping me on that," Faldo said, referring to his putting, which he said was the only part of his game that concerned him this week.

"I'm going to spend most of my time working on my putting," said Faldo, who three-putted only once last year on Augusta's big, rolling greens, which many players say are the fastest and trickiest they play all year.
"I've got three days to get ready," Faldo said just before his practice putting session.
Faldo, of course, won last year's Masters by shooting five- under-par 67 -- the lowest round of the day -- while Greg Norman was blowing a five-shot lead with an astounding 78 on Sunday.

The big Briton, who turns 40 in July, already has won more Masters than all but five golfers and only Jack Nicklaus with six and Arnold Palmer with four have won more than Faldo, who shares three victories with Sam Snead, Jimmy Demaret and gary Player of South Africa.
But Faldo, who also has won three British Open championships, dearly wants to match Palmer's four green jackets -- and perhaps challenge Nicklaus for the most.

He still has time. Nicklaus, after all, won his sixth green jacket in 1986 at age 46 and there have been four other winners in their 40s -- Ben Hogan, 40, in 1953, Sam Snead, 41, in 1954, Player, 42, in 1978 and Ben Crenshaw, 43, in 1995.
You're only as old as you feel and at Augusta you're only as good as you putt, which Faldo knows well.
